Hi Rajiv —

Thanks, and great to hear. High level we need a short set of items to create a vendor record and issue a PO:

Must-haves for PO and payment processing:
- Company registration (verified company name matching invoice)
- National tax registration (GST certificate you attached is perfect)
- Bank details + bank letter (for wire set-up)
- Completed supplier onboarding form (I attached our 1-page packet)

Tax documentation (to handle US withholding and EU VAT where applicable):
- W-8BEN-E: for non-US entities this helps establish foreign status and claim treaty benefits so we avoid default withholding on US-sourced payments. Please note: if services are performed entirely outside the US, withholding often does not apply, but we need the form on file.
- If you plan to invoice EU customers or work that is taxed in the EU, we may need your EU VAT registration or a statement about place of supply so our accounting can apply reverse-charge rules correctly.

I've attached: redwood_supplier_onboarding_packet.pdf and our standard redwood_PO_template.docx (we can create a PO once vendor record is live).

Next steps:
1) Please upload the GST cert + bank letter + completed supplier packet to the vendor portal link below (or send via secure upload).
2) Fill and return the W-8BEN-E if you want Redwood to evaluate withholding exemptions. If you prefer, we can onboard first and chase the form before the first payment.
3) Marissa will coordinate the PO timeline; Dev will confirm any special contracting/tax clauses.

Portal: https://app.procure.redwood.com/vendor-onboard/AeroCloudGlobal

Let me know if you want a short 30-minute call to walk through the fields — happy to set up.

Best,

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 11:30:00 -0700

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Subject: RE: Supplier onboarding: tax docs + PO path

Rajiv —

Thanks for the uploads and the packet. A few quick clarifications from legal & tax to make onboarding frictionless:

1) W-8BEN-E: correct that it's US-focused, but it is the standard way for a non-US vendor to document foreign status and claim any treaty benefits if Redwood makes payments that are US-source. Even if services are performed entirely from India, we still request W-8BEN-E on file. The form does not obligate you to US tax; it just documents status. If AeroCloud prefers, you can deliver the form after the vendor record is created — we will not net any taxes at the PO stage without review.

2) Withholding: generally, services performed outside the US are not US-source and therefore no withholding. However, each invoice will be evaluated by accounting against the form.

3) EU VAT / reverse charge: if AeroCloud invoices Redwood for services and the place of supply is the EU, reverse charge may apply and Redwood will account for VAT (we typically ask vendors to include the EU customer's VAT number on the invoice if available). If you do not have the EU VAT number for the end customer, leave the VAT field blank and our finance team will apply the appropriate accounting treatment.

4) PO & payment timing: once Naomi confirms the vendor record, Marissa will approve and a PO will issue. Standard payment terms for first-time international vendors: NET 30 after invoice + successful bank verification. Please ensure wire details match the bank letter to avoid delays.

5) Next step for AeroCloud: please complete the W-8BEN-E (if comfortable) and confirm whether you can include EU customer VAT numbers on relevant invoices. We will proceed with vendor creation in the portal today.

If helpful, I can connect you to our tax advisor for a 20-minute call to walk through the treaty/withholding considerations.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Head of Legal & Procurement, Redwood Inference
Attachments: W-8BEN-E-guidance.pdf
